title: WPMS/1352/2021 of DEEPAK BANSAL Vs SHARAD KUMAR GUPTA

COURT'S OR JUDGES'S ORDERS
WPMS No.1352 of 2021
Hon 'b le Sh ar ad Ku m ar Sh ar m a, J.
 (Via video conferencing).
Mr. Sagar Kothari, Advocate, for the
petitioner.
Mr. Sudhir Kumar, Advocate, for the
Caveator.
The respondent No.1, herein, is the
landlord, who had initiated the proceedings
under Section 21 (1) (a) of the Act No.13 of
1972, by instituting a PA Case No.10 of 2019,
"Sharad Kumar Gupta Vs. Kaushalya Bansal
and others", wherein, he has sought the release
of the tenement shop, by invoking the
provisions under Section 21 (1) (a) of the Act
No.13 of 1972, in relation to a shop, which was
more particularly described at the foot of the
release application, which was filed on
12.09.2019.
Before dealing with the arguments
extended by the learned counsel for the
petitioner, this Court feels it to be apt to record
the objection, which has been raised by the
learned counsel for the caveator about the
manner and the modalities which had been
adopted by the petitioner for approaching to

this Court, while giving a challenge to the
impugned order, by virtue of which the
Prescribed Authority has declined to hold the
commission, under Order 26 Rule 9 of CPC.
 It has been argued by the learned counsel
for the caveator Mr. Sudhir Kumar that earlier a
writ petition being WPMS No.3725 of 2019,
"Sharad Kumar Gupta Vs. Kaushalya
Bansal" was preferred by the landlord,
wherein, by exercising the powers under Rule
15 (3), the Court disposed of the writ petition
way back on 07.12.2019, directing to expedite
the proceedings of the release application, in
terms of Rule 15 (3), of the Rules framed under
Act No.13 of 1972. However, the proceedings
were kept on lingering and later on an extension
was sought for by the Judicial Officer, on the
administrative side, the Court has passed a fresh
order of extension of time on 28.05.2021, by
cautioning the Judicial Officer that such
slackness in deciding the matter, despite of the
orders of the Court is not appreciated.
Today, the writ petition has been
preferred by the petitioner/tenant, wherein, he
has put a challenge to the impugned order dated
22.06.2021, which was passed by the learned
Prescribed Authority in the said PA case,
whereby his Application Paper No.64A under
Order 26 Rule 9 of CPC, for holding the survey
commission has been rejected.

In fact, if the propriety of the Application
Paper No.64A, itself is taken into consideration,
it was on the pretext, that the tenant has come
up with a case that the landlord has got other
vacant accommodations available with him in
the same premises, and that fact was required to
be elaborated in the proceedings before the
Prescribed Authority. In order to substantiate
the arguments of the bonafide requirement of
the landlord. It is this application, which has
been rejected, and now has been put to
challenge in the present writ petition.
It is a settled law that the proceedings
under the Act No.13 of 1972, are summary in
nature, and which is to be decided based on the
evidence, which is to be adduced by the parties
by filing the affidavits.
The sole burden about the availability of
the other vacant accommodation with the
landlord was to be discharged by the tenant
himself by filing an appropriate evidence, based
on the assessment of the Municipal Board or by
any other mode, but not by way of holding a
commission by invoking the provisions
contained under Order 26 Rule 9 of the CPC,
which principally as per my opinion of this
Court would not be applicable in the light of the
purpose of Section 34 to be read with Rule 22
under the Act, where holding of a commission
is altogether contemplated under different

context and circumstances.
 There the commission is not permitted
for the purpose of retrieving an evidence, for a
party to built up a case, particularly, in the
instant case when the petitioner himself has not
disclosed the material fact about the earlier
orders passed by this Court, this Court declines
to exercise its discretionary jurisdiction in the
exercise of its supervisory jurisdiction under
Article 227 of the Constitution of India.
Hence the writ petition lacks merit and
the same is hereby dismissed.

( Sh ar ad Ku m ar Sh ar m a, J.)
 16.07.2021
NR/
